I've been wearing school uniforms since I started middle school last year. I admit that it isn't always fun. I have a closet full of nice, fashionable clothes, and it's frustrating that my friends at school can't see me wearing them.
However, I understand why my school has rules about uniforms. At school, students need to focus on studying. If they were always talking about fashion, it would be distracting.
Also, I think that school uniforms help prevent bullying. If we didn't have uniforms, many students would be picked on for having old-fashioned clothes.
Having uniforms also stops students from misbehaving. Without uniforms, some students would wear inappropriate clothes that would offend students and teachers.

Lastly, while I agree that uniforms make students conform, we can still find many ways to be creative. Many of my friends accessorize their uniforms with jewelry, ribbons and hair bands. Even boys wear different hats and shoes.

In conclusion, school uniforms may make students less creative, but they help us focus on schoolwork. I think that's a fair trade. Plus, they push us to be even more creative about how we express ourselves.

I go to middle school in the USA, and my school doesn't have uniforms. I don't know what I would do if we had that rule. I spend a lot of time thinking about what to wear, and I can't imagine giving that up.

Some people say that kids disrupt class when they wear inappropriate clothing. I don't think this is true, because my school has a dress code. Shirts with bad words or offensive pictures are not allowed.
I think students are much happier at school when they can wear the clothes they want.

I also think that school uniforms are a cultural difference between countries. They may be a good idea in places like Korea and Japan, but not in the USA. American kids don't want to conform to their school's idea of how they should look.
